Below is a short analysis and two *SEARCH/REPLACE* edits (one for the un-minified file and one for the minified file) that add the “@” character into the BASIC string‐literal character class so that `"@Code"` will be recognized as one string.

---

Bug root cause  
– In `components/prism-basic.js` (and its minified counterpart) the regex for string literals is  
```js
/"(?:""|[!#$%&'()*,\/:;<=>?^_ +\-.A-Z\d])*"/i
```
which does not include “@” in the character class. Any VB-string containing “@” will therefore break out of the literal match.

Fix: add “@” into the character class just after `_`.

---

<<<<<<< SEARCH

    'string': {
        // Added '@' into the character class so that VB strings like "@Code" are properly matched
        pattern: /"(?:""|[!#$%&'()*,\/:;<=>?^_@ +\-.A-Z\d])*"/i,
        greedy: true
    },
>>>>>>> REPLACE

With these two small changes, VB-Net strings containing “@” will once again be highlighted correctly.
